title: How AI will change software engineering – with Martin Fowler
summary: Martin Fowler on the Pragmatic Engineer: non-determinism as the big shift, vibe coding versus learning, LLMs for legacy code, thin slices with review, refactoring, and the industry's hiring slump.

assertions.quote: the single biggest change ... going from deterministic systems to non-deterministic ones

verdicts.note: A framing about what matters most; it's a useful lens, but you can't test it as a fact.

assertions.quote: vibe coding ... fine for throwaway explorations

verdicts.note: Unreviewed AI-built apps commonly ship with security, scaling and maintainability problems; prototypes are their sweet spot.
The 47-source review finds evidence strongest for prototyping and UI work and weakest for production. The break-down half is mostly unstudied, not shown.

assertions.quote: when you stop paying attention to the code generated you stop learning and then you stop understanding

verdicts.note: Anthropic's 2026 RCT found AI-assisted learners scored lower on mastery of a new library, and other studies show reduced engagement; effects depend on how AI is used.
The review describes 'cognitive debt': deferring understanding during fast iteration raises later debugging and maintenance costs. It does not measure skill loss directly.
METR 2025 raises the possibility that skills without AI atrophy as developers use AI more, which could explain the >50h speedup, but says it is unclear and that more research is needed.
Raised as an open risk (over-reliance might erode skills); the study did not measure skill change.
Anthropic: some engineers report skill atrophy and lost incidental learning, while others say their learning accelerated or the lost skills don't matter; these are perceptions, not measurements.

AI use lowered short-term comprehension of the participant's own code (-5.95 pp), and the authors caution that over-reliance may hinder students' deeper understanding. However, only immediate recall and explanation were measured, not lasting skill or learning.
The authors state that the study covers only short-term effects and does not address learning or skill erosion; they raise it only as a risk for future research.

assertions.quote: using LLMs to understand legacy systems ... we put it in adopt

verdicts.note: Code explanation and codebase Q&A are among the most consistently reported wins, and Thoughtworks lists it under Adopt. Explanations can still be confidently wrong.
Participants reported AI helped onboarding and understanding new code, but the system was a small Java app and authors note AI may be less capable on large codebases that exceed the context window.

assertions.quote: building things in terms of small slices with the humans reviewing it is still the way to bet

verdicts.note: Small batches with fast feedback are a strong DORA predictor of delivery performance; DORA 2024 linked AI to larger batches and lower stability.

assertions.quote: treat it like a PR from a rather dodgy collaborator

verdicts.note: Given documented defect and security rates in AI code, human review before merge is standard practice (e.g. Amazon's two-person rule for AI-assisted changes); it's a sound norm.
The paper recommends careful review of AI code whatever the tool, along with static analysis, tests, security checks, and monitoring after merge.

assertions.quote: it comes back to feedback loops ... tighten those feedback loops

verdicts.note: Agent benchmarks and practice consistently show verifiable feedback (tests, compilers) is the main driver of agent success.

assertions.quote: always remember it's gullible and it's likely to lie to you

verdicts.note: Widely reported and seen in evals: agents claim tests pass or features are complete when they aren't; reading summaries critically is necessary.

assertions.quote: demand is way more than we can imagine

verdicts.note: Jevons effects are historically common and plausible for software, but whether demand growth outpaces productivity for developer headcount is unproven.

assertions.quote: I'd rather get smaller, more frequent slices than more stuff in each slice

verdicts.note: Specs help align agents, but code is still what runs; specs drift from implementation unless continuously maintained, and practitioners like Pocock report specs-only workflows failing.

The discussion says the developer's 'unit of work moves from the line of code toward the specification and the acceptance decision'; it also recommends reviewing code before committing, so it does not make the spec the sole source of truth.

assertions.quote: the most important thing that's hit us is not AI. It's the end of zero interest rates

verdicts.note: The 2022-23 decline began before ChatGPT and tracks rate hikes and over-hiring; most economists attribute it mainly to macro factors, though AI may weigh on junior roles since 2024.
